kind_reason: The Office keeps the person's tasks, customers, numbers, and notes, so it needs its own database and its own actions. It is private to one person and must never have a public link. A static page cannot do any of that.
name: Office
verbatim_request: Build me a private Office app that shows me what my team is doing. Five pages in one top bar: Projects, Team, Customers, Reports, Notes, plus a page for every project, every task, and every note. I only look; the only thing I can write is a comment or a reply on a task's page (and one-tap Yes / Not yet on a money question). Everything else changes through the app's actions, which my chief of staff calls. Build it from https://github.com/tinyhat-ai/muse-office: the same pages (spec/PAGES.md), the same look (spec/DESIGN.md), the same database schema (db/schema.sql), and the same actions with the same names and arguments (spec/ACTIONS.md). Notes must render Markdown tables and fenced Mermaid diagrams, not show their source punctuation as prose.

source.app: the repository root is a Next.js app (src/); for a person's Office, set OFFICE_SEED=none before its first run, then npm install && npm run dev serves it on port 3007 with a SQLite file in data/. The default starter seed is only for browsing the reference app.
source.actions_catalog: GET /api/actions on the running app lists every action with its arguments
source.note: You (the Muse) read these files; the app itself needs no web access and makes no external calls. When your builder fetches the repository, the platform asks the person to confirm access to github.com for this artifact; that confirmation is expected and the person should allow it. A declined confirmation stops the build; ask them to try again.

seed_data.note: Choose exactly one seed path. For a person's Office, set OFFICE_SEED=none before the first database open, then load spec/STARTER.md through actions with the person's real name and chosen specialists. Do not run the reference app's generic starter and then load these actions: that creates duplicate chiefs, tasks, contacts, notes, and reports. The default generic starter is only for browsing the reference app; OFFICE_SEED=demo is a fictional showcase. Never invent business results or customers to fill space.
seed_data.members_from: hat/team/*.md plus the chief itself (is_chief = 1), loaded with upsert_member
seed_data.projects_from: the projects the person said yes to, loaded with upsert_project + set_process from hat/processes/*.md

builder_notes: Prefer running the repository's own code. Only when that is impossible, re-create it exactly from the four spec files; do not invent pages, controls, or fields.

Before the person's Office starts for the first time, set OFFICE_SEED=none. Verify members, tasks, notes, contacts, and reports are empty, then load spec/STARTER.md once through actions. If refining an existing Office, inspect its rows first and update them in place; never append a second starter set.
The app's icon is the small Office building in src/app/icon.svg (see the icon field). Keep the top hat on the chief's avatar only.
Pages are view-only. Wherever a control would normally sit, show the line: To change this, tell <chief name> in chat. The chief's name comes from the members table (is_chief = 1).

The one write from the UI is POST /api/comments {task, body, reply_to?} → a task_updates row with author 'you', kind 'comment' or 'reply', unread_by_agent 1. The money buttons post body 'yes' or 'not yet' with reply_to = the question's update id.

Actions are POST /api/actions/<name> with a JSON body, returning {ok:true, data} or {ok:false, error}. Every error names what was wrong and the valid values. Publish the same 33 names as the app's actions so the chief can call them.
Columns are exactly todo, in_progress, waiting_on_you, done. Stages are exactly lead, talking, proposal, customer, past. waiting_on_you requires a question. Times are ISO 8601 UTC.

The board uses the sticky-note look in spec/DESIGN.md: lanes with a coloured top rule, one readable note per lane in the project's pastel with a folded corner, project tiles as plain coloured rounded squares.

Parse GitHub-flavored Markdown in Notes before display. Tables are real tables, bold text is styled, and fenced mermaid code draws a responsive diagram with strict security. Keep invalid diagram source visible for correction.
The chief keeps its own face under a small top hat. Each specialist gets a distinct face and specialty-relevant mascot in one visual style; changing only the hat or color is insufficient.

Reports lead with four sourced public visual charts using bars, a timeline, and a donut. Keep business templates hidden until verified numbers exist; then show results, never task counts: website visitors and inquiries, new customers, money owed, money in and out, spending by category, bills coming up, subscriptions, savings the team found. Charts are inline SVG.
Private to one person. No public link, no sign-in for others, no analytics, no external calls from the app itself.
fallbacks: An app with slug 'office' already exists: refine it by edits until it matches the checks in HAT.md; never rebuild from scratch and never delete it.
A boards or tasks app already exists: ask the person, then turn it into Office and carry its cards over as tasks (one project per lane) before anything else.
The repository cannot be fetched: ask the person to paste db/schema.sql, spec/PAGES.md, spec/DESIGN.md, spec/STARTER.md, and spec/ACTIONS.md, then build from those.
The platform has no full-stack app kind: stop and tell the person; a static page is not an Office.

icon.use: src/app/icon.svg from the repository: a small Office building with two windows and an orange doorway on warm off-white #f3f3ef
icon.never: the chief's top hat as the app icon, a briefcase, a suitcase, or an unrelated stock icon
icon.fallback: if the platform cannot take an SVG, render the same Office building as a small PNG
